responses.tool-purpose: Synthesizes uploaded source material into summaries, questions, and study support.
responses.problem-solved: It helps learners and educators work across several documents without losing track of source evidence.
responses.feature-interest: Using uploaded documents to create a concise summary and source-grounded revision prompts.
responses.test-request: We uploaded notes on formative assessment and asked NotebookLM to summarise key themes and generate revision questions.
responses.test-what-happened: It produced a coherent summary with source-aware prompts and clearer links back to evidence than expected.
responses.surprised: The source-grounding reduced hallucination more effectively than in other chat-based tools.
responses.corrected: We still checked a few claims and adjusted one question that was too broad for our module context.

strengths.text: Keeps responses visibly tied to uploaded source material.
Useful for summarising multiple texts into one study view.

weaknesses.text: Output quality depends heavily on the quality of uploaded sources.

opportunities.text: Could support revision packs and seminar preparation from reading bundles.

threats.text: Students may over-rely on summaries instead of reading original sources carefully.

responses.learning-improve: It could help learners navigate a larger reading set and identify the most relevant ideas more quickly.
responses.teacher-time: Summarising document sets and drafting evidence-based revision prompts.
responses.avoid-use: Avoid it when students need to practise close reading of the original source itself.
responses.check-before-use: Check that summaries do not overstate claims and that cited evidence really supports the output.

quadrant-map.rationale: It offers strong learning value with manageable risk when source material is chosen carefully.

responses.ai-decisions: It decided which themes to foreground, which evidence to connect, and how to structure the summary.
responses.human-judgement-needed: Educators still need to judge whether the summary reflects the course emphasis and reading priorities.
responses.concerned: Students might skip the original texts and accept the notebook summary as complete understanding.
responses.other-educators-know: Its value is strongest when the source pack is carefully curated and expectations for verification are explicit.
responses.view-change: We became more confident in it once we saw how clearly it linked responses back to uploaded materials.
